clue.text: They may save us having car accidents

definitions.text: They may save us having car accidents

parts.words: They may save us having car accidents
parts.note: the clue reads as a plain description of protective straps worn in a motor car, with a hint that they spare us from crashes

explanation.surface: Some safety device spares motorists from the worst of a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps fastened across a car's occupants are designed to protect them in a collision.

clue.text: Proverbially at the bottom of all humour

definitions.text: Proverbially at the bottom of all humour

parts.words: Proverbially at the bottom of all humour
parts.note: the proverb calls this mocking irony the lowest form of wit, so it sits at the bottom of humour's ranks

explanation.surface: A saying claims something lies beneath every kind of joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the bottom of' looks like 'underlying', but it means lowest-ranked: the saying is that this is the lowest form of wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverb: mocking irony is called the lowest form of wit.

clue.text: It isn't clear how we become unconscious

definitions.text: isn't clear
definitions.meaning: a dim or indistinct mark or sound is hard to make out

definitions.text: become unconscious
definitions.meaning: a verb sense: to pass out, swoon

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure how people lose consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means dim or indistinct; as a verb it means to swoon or pass out.

clue.text: Long to be out of the headlines, as it were

definitions.text: Long to be out of the headlines, as it were

parts.words: Long to be out of the headlines, as it were
parts.note: the clue reads like a wish to avoid publicity, but describes long locks: lines growing out of the head

explanation.surface: A celebrity yearns to stay out of the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a verb (yearn), but it is an adjective: long hair, which grows in lines out of the head, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: Long locks of hair hang down from the head like lines from it.

clue.text: Tries to find oil!

definitions.text: Tries to find oil!

parts.words: Tries to find oil!
parts.note: holes drilled into the ground are attempts to strike oil, and the word also hints at the sense tiresome

explanation.surface: A prospector keeps trying to strike oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Holes drilled into the earth by prospectors searching for oil or water are given this name.

clue.text: The country that has produced some of the world's best paintings

definitions.text: The country that has produced some of the world's best paintings

parts.words: The country that has produced some of the world's best paintings
parts.note: the clue seems to name a nation famous for art, but means countryside as a subject that painters depict

explanation.surface: Some nation is said to have produced the finest artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like a nation such as Italy or Holland; it is the countryside, a painter's scenic subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings of the countryside form a genre named after views of rural scenery.

clue.text: Captain has no problem with flowers being unloaded here, presumably!

definitions.text: Captain has no problem with flowers being unloaded here, presumably!

parts.words: Captain has no problem with flowers being unloaded here, presumably!
parts.note: a ship's master unloads cargo at a harbour town; the letters of PROTEAS, a kind of flower, also unload into it

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is happy for a cargo of flowers to be discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: Proteas are South African flowers, and their letters rearranged spell the harbour, a joke on 'unloaded'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town where ships dock and cargo is discharged.

clue.text: Get plenty of land like this!

definitions.text: Get plenty of land like this!

parts.words: Get plenty of land like this!
parts.note: the exclamation reads as advice to acquire acreage, but describes soil that yields plenty of crops

explanation.surface: An encouragement to buy up a lot of property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get plenty of land' looks like advice on buying acres; it means land that gets plenty, i.e. yields abundant crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Productive soil yields abundant harvests, so such land produces plenty.

clue.text: A soldier's farewell party!

definitions.text: A soldier's farewell party!

parts.words: A soldier's farewell party!
parts.note: a send-off celebration in surface, but the group of riflemen who carry out a military execution

explanation.surface: Comrades throw a leaving do for a departing soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a celebration; it is a group, the detail that executes a condemned soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Group of soldiers detailed to carry out an execution by shooting, a grim last goodbye.

clue.text: For London Airport taxis, for instance?

definitions.text: For London Airport taxis, for instance?

parts.words: For London Airport taxis, for instance?
parts.note: taxis looks like cabs, but here it is the verb: aircraft taxi along these strips

explanation.surface: Something is provided for cabs serving Heathrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxis' looks like cabs; read it as the verb, what aircraft do when moving along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of paved ground at an airport along which aircraft move, take off and land.

clue.text: Release, in or around a place in Africa

definitions.text: a place in Africa

indicators.note: around signals the letters of the preceding words are moved about into a new order

parts.words: Release
in
or

explanation.surface: An instruction to set something free, inside or nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' looks like the instruction of the surface, but it is anagram fodder along with 'in' and 'or', all three words rearranged by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: A country on the west coast of Africa, with Freetown as its capital.

clue.text: Cook ducks, perhaps, without water-chestnuts; that's how they're often served!

definitions.text: Cook ducks, perhaps, without water-chestnuts; that's how they're often served!

parts.words: Cook ducks, perhaps, without water-chestnuts; that's how they're often served!
parts.note: the clue reads as a recipe instruction; ducks are commonly served oven-cooked in this way

explanation.surface: A cook is advised to prepare duck plainly, without a Chinese garnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking in an oven by dry heat, the usual way poultry is served.

clue.text: A lot of seaside rock made from it?

definitions.text: A lot of seaside rock made from it?

parts.words: A lot of seaside rock made from it?
parts.note: seaside rock is a British stick of candy sold at resorts, but here it means cliffs and beach stone

explanation.surface: A question about what the sugary rock sold at resorts is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a hard sugar stick sold at British resorts; here it is literal rock, which at the coast is often made of compacted grains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedimentary stone formed of compacted grains of the beach material.

clue.text: One or two are listed in the Pentateuch

definitions.text: One or two are listed in the Pentateuch

parts.words: One or two are listed in the Pentateuch
parts.note: one and two are figures, and the fourth of the five books of Moses has this title

explanation.surface: A few things are recorded in the first five books of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or two' looks like 'a few'; it gives examples of figures, and the Pentateuch's fourth book bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fourth book of the Pentateuch; one and two are examples of figures.

clue.text: Ornament material!

definitions.text: Ornament material!

parts.words: Ornament material!
parts.note: read as an instruction to decorate fabric, which describes stitching designs onto cloth with a needle

explanation.surface: A decorative fabric, or a call to decorate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ornament material' looks like a noun phrase (decorative cloth); read 'ornament' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorating cloth with needlework designs, a verb for adorning fabric.

clue.text: Separate people In the crowd

definitions.text: Separate people In the crowd

parts.words: Separate people In the crowd
parts.note: a command to break up a gathering; to disperse in different directions

explanation.surface: Police are told to split up members of a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersing a crowd means throwing its members apart in all directions.

clue.text: They opposed Christ being associated with Pharisees

definitions.text: They opposed Christ being associated with Pharisees

parts.words: They opposed Christ being associated with Pharisees
parts.note: the Gospels repeatedly pair the Pharisees with the teachers of Jewish law who opposed Jesus

explanation.surface: Some objected to Jesus keeping company with the Pharisees.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests objecting to Christ's company; read it as: those who opposed Christ, and who are linked with Pharisees in the Gospel phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel phrase pairs these teachers of the law with the Pharisees as Jesus's opponents.

clue.text: Taking in work from an author

definitions.text: Taking in work from an author

parts.words: Taking in work from an author
parts.note: absorbing a writer's book by eye, or receiving a manuscript to assess for a publisher

explanation.surface: An editor accepts a manuscript from a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Perusing a book means absorbing an author's work through the eyes.

clue.text: Person pretending not to deserve this honourable name

definitions.text: Person pretending not to deserve this honourable name

parts.words: Person pretending not to deserve this honourable name
parts.note: someone who pretends is false and does not merit being called genuine; the clue also hints at a pretender being in-whatever-the-word-is

explanation.surface: A fraud is unworthy of an honourable title.
explanation.walkthrough: A pretender is insincere, which is precisely 'not' this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and honest in feeling, the opposite of a pretender.

clue.text: Beat vile rap and come out on top!

definitions.text: come out on top

indicators.note: to beat something is to batter it out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.words: vile
rap

explanation.surface: Someone defeats nasty music and triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like 'defeat'; it rearranges VILE and RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To win through, to triumph over opposition.

clue.text: Made from ingredients in the kitchen cabinet, perhaps

definitions.text: Made from ingredients in the kitchen cabinet, perhaps

parts.words: Made from ingredients in the kitchen cabinet, perhaps
parts.note: cabinet looks like a cupboard, but cabinet is the name of a traditional steamed British dessert

explanation.surface: A dish is made from what is in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Cabinet pudding is an old British steamed dessert of sponge, fruit and custard, so the cabinet is the dish, not the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert course; cabinet is one traditional British steamed variety.

clue.text: Damned soul due for expulsion is cracking nuts

definitions.text: nuts

indicators.note: these words say the letters of the following word are to be thrown out of the pool
cracking breaks the pool apart so its remaining letters can be rearranged, as a nut's shell is broken

parts.words: Damned soul
due

explanation.surface: A lost soul awaiting expulsion is busy cracking nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of DAMNED SOUL, remove those of DUE ('for expulsion'), and rearrange the rest ('cracking') to get the nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible kernels of the almond tree are a familiar type of nut.

clue.text: Women are without make-up or jewellery round Aden way

definitions.text: without make-up or jewellery

indicators.note: the Aden way suggests a different style or manner, so the preceding letters are arranged in another fashion

parts.words: round
Aden

explanation.surface: Women near Aden go without cosmetics or jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a preposition placing women near Aden, a port city in Yemen; it is fodder, rearranged with Aden by 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and undecorated, with no ornament or embellishment added.

clue.text: Christened one who wasn't here "late for the dance"

definitions.text: Christened one who wasn't here "late for the dance"

parts.words: Christened one who wasn't here "late for the dance"
parts.note: in Catholic tradition unbaptised souls went to this borderland, so a christened person wasn't there; it is also a Caribbean dance under a bar

explanation.surface: A baptised person missed out by arriving late to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: In Catholic teaching unbaptised infants went to this state, so the christened were never there; it is also the dance where one leans back under a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Theological borderland of the unbaptised, and also a Caribbean dance done under a lowered bar.

clue.text: £999; it is the maximum set by the bank manager!

definitions.text: the maximum set by the bank manager

parts.note: the pound sign comes from L for libra, the Latin pound
in Roman numerals 999 can be written IM, one before a thousand

parts.words: it
parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bank manager sets an overdraft ceiling of nine hundred and ninety-nine pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: IM for 999 is a non-standard Roman numeral (one less than M, a thousand).
explanation.definitionFit: A credit ceiling or cap that a bank imposes on borrowing.

clue.text: What we have to drop like this!

definitions.text: What we have to drop like this!

parts.words: What we have to drop like this!
parts.note: things that drop gradually shrink away; also, the letters of the word lose their WE when dropped

explanation.surface: Something we own must be reduced in this manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink or diminish gradually, as supplies do.

clue.text: Me&mine's trouble can become very great

definitions.text: very great

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up or disturb, so the preceding letters are churned into a new order

parts.words: Me&mine's
parts.note: the words me and mine's give their letters with the S kept

explanation.surface: My family's problems could grow enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ME, MINE and the S of 'mine's' (seven letters).
explanation.definitionFit: Huge, vast or enormous in size or degree.

clue.text: May have bars that are opened for visitors to horticultural show!

definitions.text: May have bars that are opened for visitors to horticultural show!

parts.words: May have bars that are opened for visitors to horticultural show!
parts.note: bars suggest pubs at a fair, but here they are the rails of entrances opened to let visitors into the grounds

explanation.surface: A flower show may have drinking bars open to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like drinking places at a show; they are the rails of entrances into a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred entrances into a garden, swung open to admit visitors.
